title: The comparison and finitude of proper direct images
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic prime to $N$, let $\Lambda$ be
the finite commutative ring annihilated by $N$ of
[sbc-def-coefficient-conventions], let $S$ be of finite type over
$k$, let $f:X\to S$ be a
proper morphism whose
geometric fibres have
dimension at most $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, and let $F$ be a
constructible
$\Lambda$-sheaf on $X_{{\mathrm{et}}}$. Then:

1. **(i)** (*the comparison*) For every $q\geq0$ and every
geometric point
$\bar s$ of $S$, the comparison map of
[cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite]
$$
(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
H^q\bigl(X_{\bar s},F|_{X_{\bar s}}\bigr)
$$
is an isomorphism; each fibre-cohomology group
$H^q(X_{\bar s},F|_{X_{\bar s}})$ is a finite $\Lambda$-module;
and these groups vanish for $q>2d$.
1. **(ii)** (*the finitude*) The higher direct images
$R^qf_*F$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] are
constructible
on $S_{{\mathrm{et}}}$ for every $q\geq0$, and
$R^qf_*F=0$ for $q>2d$.

proof.text: First, $X$ is of finite type over $k$. Indeed, properness includes finite type by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Choose a finite affine cover $S=\bigcup_i\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, with each $A_i$ finitely generated over $k$, and finite affine covers $f^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A_i)=\bigcup_j\operatorname{Spec}B_{ij}$, with each $B_{ij}$ finitely generated over $A_i$. The images of generators of $A_i$ together with generators of $B_{ij}$ over $A_i$ generate $B_{ij}$ over $k$. These finitely many affine opens cover $X$, proving finite type directly from the definition. Since $N$ is prime to the characteristic of $k$, it is invertible on these $k$-schemes, as required by the coefficient conventions. Thus [thm-fin-proper-constructibility-complete] applies to $f$ and gives $\mathcal C(f)$. Unfolding [def-finrepair-property-c], every $R^qf_*F$ is constructible on $S_{{\mathrm{et}}}$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-stalks], every geometric stalk of $F$ is finite. Thus $F$ is a finite sheaf in exactly the sense of [def-constructible-finite], so the finite-sheaf clause of [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] applies to the proper morphism $f$. For every geometric point $\bar s$ and every $q\geq0$ it gives the canonical comparison isomorphism $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X_{\bar s},F|_{X_{\bar s}})$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-stalks] again, now to $R^qf_*F$, which is constructible by step 1: its stalk at $\bar s$ is finite. The displayed $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism therefore proves that the fibre-cohomology group is a finite $\Lambda$-module.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph (proper base change and finite fibres)

proof.text: Write $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. By clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], the base change $X_{\bar s}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is proper; hence it is of finite type by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Its dimension is at most $d$ by the hypothesis on every geometric fibre, and $N$ remains invertible over the field extension $k\to\Omega$. Apply [prop-constructible-pullback] to $i_{\bar s}:X_{\bar s}\to X$: the inverse image $i_{\bar s}^{-1}F=F|_{X_{\bar s}}$ is constructible. All hypotheses of [fin4-lem-fibrewise-cohomological-dimension] now hold with $k'=\Omega$, so $H^q(X_{\bar s},F|_{X_{\bar s}})=0$ for every $q>2d$. Under the comparison isomorphism of step 2, its zero target forces $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}=0$ for every geometric point $\bar s$ and every $q>2d$.

For $q>2d$, apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to the underlying abelian-sheaf morphism of $0\to R^qf_*F$. By step 3 its map on every geometric stalk is an isomorphism (both source and target stalks are zero), so this is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. Its inverse respects the $\Lambda$-action: for a local section $s$ and scalar $a$, applying the original injective $\Lambda$-linear map to the inverse image of $as$ and to $a$ times the inverse image of $s$ gives $as$ in both cases. Hence the inverse is $\Lambda$-linear and $R^qf_*F=0$ as a module sheaf. Step 1 already supplied constructibility for every $q\ge0$ and step 2 supplied the finite fibre groups.
